CNAME.why: RR type 5 in the IANA registry, universally known. Alias 'alias' is a common English word and should be dropped.

NSAP.why: RR type 22 in the IANA registry (obsolete, RFC 1348). Obscure enough for Heisenbug.

HIP.why: RR type 55 (Host Identity Protocol, RFC 8005). Known mainly to systems and networking people, so Memory leak fits.

NID.why: RR type 104 (ILNP, RFC 6742). Deep internals, so Heisenbug fits.

KX.why: RR type 36 (Key Exchanger, RFC 2230). Deep DNSSEC-adjacent detail, so Heisenbug fits.

URI.why: RR type 256 (RFC 7553). The expansion 'uniform resource identifier' is the same answer; 'URI record' is a variant. Specialist tier fits.

RT.why: RR type 21 (Route Through, RFC 1183). Deep internals, so Heisenbug fits.

OPENPGPKEY.why: RR type 61 (RFC 7929). The alias is the expansion of the same name. Specialist tier fits.

KEY.why: RR type 25 (RFC 2535), obsolete DNSSEC predecessor of DNSKEY. Heisenbug is defensible for an obsolete type.

NINFO.why: RR type 56 (Zone Status, draft-era). Very deep, so Heisenbug fits.

L32.why: RR type 105 (RFC 6742). Deep internals, so Heisenbug fits.

WALLET.why: I cannot confirm from the sample that WALLET is a registered TYPE number in the IANA registry. Under the strict rule, unsure means false.

PX.why: RR type 26 (X.400 mapping, RFC 2163). Deep internals, so Heisenbug fits.

CDNSKEY.why: RR type 60 (RFC 7344). DNSSEC specialists know it, so Race condition fits.

TXT.why: RR type 16, very widely known, so Off-by-one fits. Alias 'text' is a common English word and should be dropped.

DNSKEY.why: RR type 48 (RFC 4034). Known to DNS and DNSSEC operators, so Memory leak fits.

PTR.why: RR type 12, very widely known, so Off-by-one fits. Aliases 'pointer' and 'reverse' are common English words and should be dropped.

SPF.why: RR type 99 (RFC 7208), deprecated in favour of TXT. Mail and sysadmin folks know it, so Memory leak fits.

SIG.why: RR type 24 (RFC 2535), obsolete DNSSEC predecessor of RRSIG, same class as KEY. Memory leak is too shallow; Heisenbug fits better.

EUI64.why: RR type 109 (RFC 7043). Very obscure, so Heisenbug fits.
